proposed_from.topic: Graph-recursive formula-or-ambiguity certificates for fine-grid causal transfers from subsampled Gaussian process DAGs. Let X_t=A X_{t-1}+ε_t be a stable stationary Gaussian VAR(1) with positive diagonal innovation covariance and a supplied labeled lower-triangular cross-variable DAG; observe only Y_s=X_{ms}. From the identified coarse transition B=A^m and coarse innovation covariance, give a terminating sound-and-complete certificate for a queried transfer h_uv(z)=A_vu z/(1−A_vv z). Prove graph-recursive generic point identification for odd m through divided differences, the unavoidable same-law symmetry (A,D)↦(−A,D) and transfer ambiguity for even m, and a real-closed-field/CAD fallback that projects every singular compatible fiber jointly onto (A_vu,A_vv), returning either one rational transfer or two attained stable witnesses. Add Wald bands on an explicit regular class and globally honest inversion of a coarse lag-moment confidence region without branch selection. Credit classical Smith/Higham triangular-root recursion and the subsampling work of Gong et al., Tank–Fox–Shojaie, Hyttinen et al., and Gersing–Sögner–Deistler; frame Gong et al.'s Temperature–Ozone example only as a conditional m=2 Gaussian ambiguity audit under an externally defensible ordering. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the graph path expansion (A^m)_vu=A_vu C_m(A_vv,A_uu)+R, proved C_m positive off (0,0) for odd m and zero exactly at opposite persistences for even m, and verified the three-node rational witness including its indirect-path remainder. It derived the open singular fiber |a|<sqrt(q2/q1), the global even-factor sign obstruction, and the exact polynomial test for equality of full transfers. Zero diagonals, absent edges, open fibers, covariance filtering, zero-edge transfers, input encoding, branch mergers, and current collisions were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove and calibrate an explicit uniform Gaussian quadratic-form confidence region for overlapping stationary lag moments on the compact stable class, with finite-sample constants and rational outward rounding, so semialgebraic inversion has advertised global coverage. EARLY KILL TEST: Exact CAD on d=2,m=3 with B=0 and diagonal Q must return two interior transfer-distinct witnesses, and every nonzero-edge d=2,m=2 case must retain the global sign pair; any singleton, endpoint-only witness, or lost sign pair stops the launch. proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest identification comparator is Gong et al. (2015), which states general Gaussian nonuniqueness and proves recovery by non-Gaussian independent-component information. The closest algebraic comparator is Smith (2003), which computes one triangular matrix root recursively. The proposed kernel instead characterizes a target-specific Gaussian observational fiber after a supplied process DAG and the coarse innovation covariance are imposed: odd regular strata have a unique graph-recursive transfer, every even factor retains a global sign-paired ambiguity for a nonzero edge, and singular strata receive a terminating complete transfer-equality decision with attained witnesses. The inference layer is also distinct from Reiter et al. (2024): it inverts a finite-sample coarse-moment region across all branches and singularities rather than conditioning on a differentiable identified fine-grid parameter.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and its supplementary proof, and Section 6 were read. The proof identifies the mixing matrix from non-Gaussian innovations and leaves Gaussian second-order root multiplicity unresolved.
seed_details.question: For a supplied ordered process DAG and Gaussian shocks, characterize exactly when the direct transfer \(h_{uv}(z)\) is constant on the complete stable root-and-innovation fiber, with a graph recursion on regular strata and exact witnesses on singular strata.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace Gong et al.'s independent-component recovery of \([I,A,\ldots,A^{m-1}]\) by Smith's entrywise triangular-root recurrence, then retain every zero divided-difference stratum instead of selecting a root.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing subsampled Gaussian VARs with triangular roots, transfer functions, parity, and real quantifier elimination found matrix-root algorithms and broad nonidentification results, but no target-specific complete certificate.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from Gong et al. because their Theorem 2 already gives the odd-versus-even sign frontier. Rebuttal: their theorem uses non-Gaussian independent-component information, whereas this seed uses only the Gaussian coarse law, admits singular positive-dimensional fibers, filters roots by the coarse covariance, and certifies a transfer rather than the whole transition matrix.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Sections 2.2--2.3, Propositions 2.3--2.4 and their quadratic-form proof, and Section 7 were read. The paper controls Gaussian sample Gram matrices through a spectral-density envelope but does not invert a multibranch causal fiber.
seed_details.question: Can an explicit finite-sample simultaneous region for overlapping lag-zero and lag-one Gaussian moments be outward-rounded and inverted through the full root fiber to cover \(h_{uv}\) uniformly at branch collisions?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Represent both lag-zero and nonsymmetric lag-one entries as symmetric quadratic forms of one stacked Gaussian trajectory, rather than applying a sparse Gram-matrix bound only at lag zero.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for finite-sample multivariate lag-moment regions combined with semialgebraic root-fiber inversion found separate concentration and covariance-band results, but no branch-free causal-transfer inversion.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: union bounds and Hanson--Wright make this routine. Rebuttal: the load-bearing work is a common explicit covariance-operator envelope for overlapping lag products, exact rational outward rounding, and coverage-preserving inversion across singular and disconnected root fibers.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Propositions 3.2 and 4.2, the elimination-tree complexity discussion, and Section 7 were read. Chordality is preserved under a perfect elimination order, but the result is not specialized to path-filled VAR compatibility polynomials.
seed_details.question: Does ancestor closure in a supplied process DAG yield a perfect elimination order and a graph-height bound for the residual CAD problem after regular triangular coordinates are removed?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compute the correlative-sparsity graph after expanding \(A^m\) and the accumulated covariance, because directed-path monomials create fill that is absent from the original DAG.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches combining chordal CAD, matrix powers, Lyapunov-type covariance equations, and subsampled causal graphs found no bound preserving exact witness extraction.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Li et al.'s elimination-tree bound applies verbatim. Rebuttal: its premise concerns the polynomial correlative graph; proving that the powered-transition and accumulated-covariance system has controlled chordal completion is precisely the missing theorem.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1 and 4, their identification argument, and the empirical discussion were read. Their recovery without a supplied order relies on independent non-Gaussian shocks.
seed_details.question: When is \(h_{uv}\) invariant across every permutation-triangular Gaussian root compatible with the coarse law?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace non-Gaussian column matching by a finite union over topological orders, with polynomial transfer-equality tests inside each order-root cell.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found complete qualitative graph enumeration under subsampling but no numerical transfer invariance over joint order and root uncertainty.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: enumerating \(d!\) orders and invoking CAD is only brute force. Rebuttal: a publishable version needs an order-invariance criterion or symmetry quotient; without it the seed is computationally correct but mathematically thin.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Theorems 1--3, the free-autocovariance construction, Theorem 6, and Section 5 were read. The paper proves generic parameter nonidentification for regular mixed-frequency VARMA models with moving-average order exceeding autoregressive order.
seed_details.question: Can an ordered graph make one rational process transfer constant along Deistler et al.'s free-autocovariance fiber even when the full VARMA parameter is not locally identified?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the transfer along the paper's open autocovariance directions and characterize when its differential annihilates the fiber tangent space before applying global algebraic elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing mixed-frequency VARMA nonidentification with target-specific process transfers found parameter-level retrieval and process-graph effect identification, but no functional refinement of the \(r>p\) boundary.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a generic free parameter will generically change every nonconstant transfer. Rebuttal: graph zeros can make a rational target orthogonal to nuisance directions, but the seed lacks a concrete nondegenerate graph family after the deeper scan.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, Sections 3.1--3.4, Theorem 1, its delta-method construction, and Section 6 were read. The paper derives Wald laws when the fine-grid SVAR effect is already a differentiable function of identified coefficients.
seed_details.question: Derive simultaneous Wald bands for \(h_{uv}\) after a smooth graph-recursive root map, with an explicit separation margin from divided-difference and branch collisions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Compose the lag-moment central limit theorem with the implicit derivative of the selected triangular root before applying the rational effect derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found local matrix-function perturbation theory and fine-grid process-effect Wald inference, but no inference after subsampling-root identification.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is a direct delta-method corollary of Reiter et al. Rebuttal: the root Jacobian and branch matching are new, but standing alone the result remains an inference appendix rather than the kernel.

seed_details.anchor_read: The Gaussian nonuniqueness discussion around Section 3.2 and the matrix-root examples were read together with the supplementary proof of Theorem 2.
seed_details.question: Characterize the topology and exact semialgebraic endpoints of transfer identified sets on zero divided-difference strata, distinguishing open pair fibers from attained transfer witnesses.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At \(C_m(A_{vv},A_{uu})=0\), stop dividing and project the residual polynomial and covariance equations jointly onto \((A_{vu},A_{vv})\).
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found no treatment of open singular root fibers filtered by diagonal fine-grid innovation covariance.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: CAD automatically describes the set, so there is no theorem. Rebuttal: the nontrivial result is the target-aware equality test and attained two-witness certificate despite open or positive-dimensional parameter fibers.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, the system-to-measurement graph map, the constraint formulation, experiments, and discussion were read. The paper allows an unknown subsampling rate for qualitative graph recovery.
seed_details.question: For \(m\) known only to lie in a finite set, decide whether \(h_{uv}\) is invariant over the union of all compatible factor-specific Gaussian fibers.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Enrich each discrete sampling-factor candidate with numerical matrix-power, covariance, stability, and transfer-equality constraints.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found unknown-rate graph compatibility but no functional certificate over numerical Gaussian root fibers.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: a finite union of already solved fixed-\(m\) certificates is immediate. Rebuttal: the cross-factor equality test is exact but does not supply enough new mathematics beyond the fixed-factor kernel.

seed_details.anchor_read: The non-Gaussian identifiability assumptions and complete SVAR identification theorem were read.
seed_details.question: Find the smallest quantified departure from Gaussianity that breaks the even global-sign transfer ambiguity, and derive a critical cumulant threshold for reliable branch discrimination.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact independent-component uniqueness by local testing between sign-paired innovation convolutions using the first nonzero odd cumulant.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found non-Gaussian exact identification and ICA perturbation results, but no observable critical threshold tailored to subsampling sign pairs.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: identifiability has no positive cumulant threshold at population level; any nonzero asymmetric cumulant may suffice. Rebuttal: a statistical detection boundary could exist, but that is a different local-asymptotic project and the proposed critical-\(\delta\) object was not yet defensible.

seed_details.anchor_read: Introduction, the blocked differencing construction, the generic identification theorem, and the conclusion were read. The paper identifies unit-root VAR parameters from mixed-frequency second moments after lagged differencing.
seed_details.question: Can cointegrating graph restrictions identify a stationary long-run causal transfer when the fine transition has a unit root and observations are subsampled?
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Apply graph recursion to the stable block after the paper's lag-\(N\) differencing and isolate the unit-root block through the cointegrating decomposition.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found unit-root parameter retrieval and stationary process-graph effects separately, but no parity certificate for cointegrating transfers.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the target \(A_{vu}z/(1-A_{vv}z)\) is singular at the unit root and is not the right long-run estimand. Rebuttal: a cointegrating transfer can be defined, but doing so changes the target beyond the present brief.
